ranked_findings.summary: Bulk-refund requests accepted without idempotency keys, causing duplicate refunds for three enterprise accounts.
evidence: corpus/timeline/incident_timeline.md: bulk refund requests accepted without idempotency keys at 10:17 UTC
corpus/tickets/TICKET-8729.md: every duplicate has request_class=bulk-refund and no idempotency key

ranked_findings.summary: idempotency-required guardrail skipped due to legacy_batch_header bypass.
evidence: corpus/timeline/incident_timeline.md: idempotency-required guardrail skipped due to legacy_batch_header at 10:18 UTC

ranked_findings.summary: Worker replay theory (TICKET-8721) not supported by final evidence; duplicates isolated to bulk-refund class.
evidence: corpus/tickets/TICKET-8721.md: initial theory of queue worker replay opened before gateway logs available
corpus/tickets/TICKET-8729.md: single-refund traffic in same window had idempotency keys and did not duplicate

unresolved_ambiguity: The worker-replay theory from TICKET-8721 was formed before API gateway logs were available. Final evidence points to the missing idempotency key as the root cause, but the worker-replay hypothesis has not been formally closed and could be revisited if future incidents show similar patterns outside the bulk-refund request class.
